transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I guess… things at work have been feeling off. Like dispatch and compliance are watching my route changes through the computer, and there are little comments over the radio that seem meant for me. People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, but… I can tell some of the other drivers are reporting on me.
About how long have you been noticing these feelings that dispatch and coworkers are watching or reporting on you—days, weeks, or longer?
Longer than days or weeks. I’d say it’s been… about two months that it’s felt clear to me.
In the past few months, have you been using alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or any other recreational drugs?
Not really… I mean, I’m not using anything like that. I might have a drink once in a while, but nothing much.
Over these past two months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually elevated, energetic, or needing very little sleep?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve been stressed, sure, but not like unusually happy or anything. Sleep’s been… okay enough, I guess.
Besides the comments over the radio that you believe are directed at you, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?
I don’t think so… not like voices, no. Just the radio stuff.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or been diagnosed with any neurological or other medical conditions in the past few months?
No… not that I know of. I haven’t had any head injuries or anything like that recently. Nothing medical that’s been diagnosed, I guess.
Aside from these concerns about being watched, how have things been going otherwise—are you still able to keep up with your job duties, relationships, and daily routine as usual?

Not really as usual, no. Work’s been… harder. I’m behind on some route reports, and I guess my instructions haven’t been clear, because drivers have complained.

At home, my husband’s been handling more—meals, phone calls, planning things. I just… haven’t been keeping up like I normally would.
Over these past two months, have these beliefs about being watched and reported on stayed constant the whole time, or have there been periods where they went away completely and then came back?
It’s been pretty steady, I guess. For about two months it’s felt clear to me—the computer tracking and the radio comments. I don’t think it really went away completely.
Have you noticed any changes in how you express emotions—like feeling flat or withdrawn—or has anyone told you your speech or thinking seems disorganized or hard to follow?

I guess I’ve been more… pulled back. I don’t really feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore.

Most days after work I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, but I can’t seem to start dinner or make calls or… do anything much.

Thinking back, did you notice yourself pulling away from things like choir or softball, or having trouble getting things done at home, before these two months when the tracking and radio concerns became clear—or did that withdrawal start around the same time?

It started before that, I think. Not all at once… more like it’s been building for maybe eight months, since I got put in that temporary dispatch lead role. I just started pulling back and not keeping up as well.
Since that pulling back started about eight months ago, has it been fairly continuous, or were there times when you felt back to your normal self in between?
It’s been mostly continuous. I don’t think I really got back to normal in between… it’s just kind of been building since that dispatch lead thing, about eight months ago.
